review_type: independent visual comparison of official product stills against parent-worktree three-quarter model previews and manufacturer/model contact sheets
scope: 14 atmosphere models currently built in the parent legacy-effects batch; MDG ATMOSPHERE APS excluded because it was not in the requested built set

status_definitions.acceptable_approximation: Overall body silhouette, major attached components and reference pose are recognizably consistent; simplified branding, fasteners, vents and small hardware are not blockers.
status_definitions.visual_review_pending: A prominent silhouette, component, count, or pose mismatch could materially misidentify the equipment or its physical envelope; parent should revise or explicitly accept before treating the model as visually reviewed.

findings.observation: The broad framed bubble-wheel array is oriented forward, with the top handle and lower body represented. The visible multi-wheel row broadly conveys the six-wheel arrangement; simplified open spiral loops differ from the source's solid patterned paddle wheels but are an acceptable detail approximation. Per request, the currently pending width/depth axis correction is not judged here.

The product is a low, strongly wedge-shaped fazer with a raised angled rear/upper panel and a projecting open outlet at the opposite end. The model reads as a rectangular closed box with a shallow top and flat end panel; its main silhouette and outlet construction do not match the source. Rework the wedge profile and open projecting outlet before visual sign-off.

The source is a distinctive large wheeled case with a raised open-top/upper cover section, a sloped exposed controls deck, projecting outlets/fan hardware, prominent front ventilation and corner hardware. The model is a generic closed flight case with a small flat top hatch and no visible wheels, sloped controls deck, or projecting equipment. The missing upper assembly and caster base materially change both silhouette and envelope.

The compact, horizontal one-piece hazer body, raised lid/handle and front outlet area are present in the correct general pose. Panel seams, tapering/chamfers, finish and model-specific lettering are simplified; these are secondary to the preserved low rectangular silhouette.

Both show an upright integrated flight-case enclosure with perimeter extrusions/corners and an open top access panel. Model hardware and case-face details are stylized, but the closed-case body form and access opening are recognizable.

The snow machine's horizontal silver chassis, tall adjustable hanging bracket, upper carry handle and forward outlet are preserved. The source has a more strongly swept lower/front shell and a deep rectangular outlet; the model rounds and squares these details, but retains the product's overall machine-and-bracket silhouette.

The source's long tapered silver body, large perforated suspension bracket and front outlet are all recognizable. Model body is more boxy and less wedge-like, with a simplified outlet, but it preserves the principal silhouette, bracket and forward-facing pose.

The tall suspension handle and angled hinged/front bubble assembly are represented, and the model faces the output forward. The source side shell is faceted and the model body is a simpler rectangular tub; source lettering and exact mounting details are omitted, without a major pose or component-count discrepancy apparent in the reviewed view.

The compact horizontal body, included tall suspension bracket, top reservoir/handle area, side ventilation and forward nozzle are present in the upright product pose. Surface embossing, reservoir and nozzle detail are simplified but the main body and mounting silhouette are consistent.

The long low silver/black chassis, top reservoir/control region, carry handles, side ventilation and forward nozzle appear in the correct general configuration. Rounded end geometry, grills, reservoir fittings and panel detail are simplified; the principal silhouette is retained.

The longer low chassis with matching top reservoir/control region, side panel and forward nozzle is present. Housing segmentation, vent layout, fittings and model-specific small details are simplified; body silhouette and pose align with the reference.

The small blue handheld rectangular unit and metal end plate/nozzle are preserved. The reference has a more detailed perforated face and visible gauge; the model instead presents side vents and a larger plain circular opening. These are detail/face-design differences on an otherwise correctly sized compact body, not a major silhouette or pose error.

The blue rectangular hazer body, black facia/end, side ventilation and broad enclosure volume are represented. The reference has an angled/stepped front facia, top handle and rear fluid canister/hose; the model omits or simplifies those recognisable but smaller accessories. The body remains recognizable, with no major pose reversal apparent.

The source's defining layout is an open side cradle carrying a conspicuous translucent fluid reservoir, a large front control/display and output bay, plus a tall U-shaped mounting bracket. The preview is a closed generic rectangular case with only a small end display, side grille and simplified bar; it has no reservoir/cradle or corresponding front/control arrangement. This removes a major attached component and changes the front/side identity; revise or explicitly approve this omission before visual sign-off.

not_assessed: dimensional correctness, export scale, DMX/control accuracy, material fidelity, rear-view completeness, B-200 width/depth correction pending in research data
